text:
Neal Pionk is back to being Winnipeg's minutes machine, at 24 a night and over 27 in two games this month, and the Jets have won seven of his last ten. Last season he managed 12 points in 51 games. This season he has 13 in 23, already past that total.

He's also been unlucky in a way that's hidden the good. Winnipeg has scored 5.4 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, which is why our numbers flag him as due: on-ice finishing that far below the chances usually swings back, and it would bring assists with it. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him moving the puck well last season, with 65% of his exits leaving the zone with possession and setup numbers in the 81st percentile.

The worry is the other end. The Jets get under 48% of the expected goals with him at five on five, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last year, with opponents' chances rising against him while he faced top competition. Watch the chances against: the points look sustainable, the defense less so.
